class.name: CameraAttributesPhysical
class.description: [CameraAttributesPhysical] is used to set rendering settings based on a physically-based camera's settings. It is responsible for exposure, auto-exposure, and depth of field. When used in a [WorldEnvironment], it provides default settings for exposure, auto-exposure, and depth of field that will be used by all cameras without their own [CameraAttributes], including the editor camera. When used in a [Camera3D], it will override any [CameraAttributes] set in the [WorldEnvironment] and will override the [Camera3D]'s [member Camera3D.far], [member Camera3D.near], [member Camera3D.fov], and [member Camera3D.keep_aspect] properties. When used in [VoxelGI] or [LightmapGI], only the exposure settings will be used. The default values are intended for use in an outdoor environment; tips for values to use in an indoor environment can be found in each setting's documentation. [b]Note:[/b] Depth of field blur is only supported in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility. [b]Note:[/b] Auto-exposure is only supported in the Forward+ rendering method, not Mobile or Compatibility.

method.name: get_fov
method.description: Returns the vertical field of view that corresponds to the [member frustum_focal_length]. This value is calculated internally whenever [member frustum_focal_length] is changed.

method.name: get_sensor_format_size
method.description: Returns the width and height in millimeters of a [enum SensorFormat], or 36x24 for [constant SENSOR_FORMAT_CUSTOM].

method.name: is_fov_horizontal
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when [method get_fov] is the horizontal field of view, which is the case for an anamorphic lens ([member lens_anamorphic_squeeze] above 1.0), and [code]false[/code] when it is the vertical one.

members.member: The maximum luminance (in EV100) used when calculating auto exposure. When calculating scene average luminance, color values will be clamped to at least this value. This limits the auto-exposure from exposing below a certain brightness, resulting in a cut off point where the scene will remain bright.

The minimum luminance (in EV100) used when calculating auto exposure. When calculating scene average luminance, color values will be clamped to at least this value. This limits the auto-exposure from exposing above a certain brightness, resulting in a cut off point where the scene will remain dark.

If [code]true[/code], the aperture's diffraction softens the image: a point spreads into an Airy disk of diameter [code]2.44 λ N[/code] (with [code]λ[/code] = 550 nm and [code]N[/code] the working f-number, larger at close focus). The blur is relative to the sensor, so it is the same fraction of the frame at any resolution, and like on a real camera it only shows at small apertures: past about f/11 on a 24-megapixel full-frame sensor, but only past f/32 or so at 1080p, whose pixels are much larger. [b]Note:[/b] Applied by the tonemap pass with 25 texture reads per pixel (75 with [member CameraAttributes.chromatic_aberration_enabled]), skipped when the blur is far below a pixel. In the Compatibility renderer it makes the scene go through the post-processing pass.
Scales the diffraction blur's size. [code]1.0[/code] is the physical amount.

Size of the aperture of the camera, measured in f-stops. An f-stop is a unitless ratio between the focal length of the camera and the diameter of the aperture. A high aperture setting will result in a smaller aperture which leads to a dimmer image and sharper focus. A low aperture results in a wide aperture which lets in more light resulting in a brighter, less-focused image. Default is appropriate for outdoors at daytime (i.e. for use with a default [DirectionalLight3D]), for indoor lighting, a value between 2 and 4 is more appropriate. Only available when [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units] is enabled.

The strength of a neutral density filter in front of the lens, in stops: each stop halves the light. Lets you use a wide aperture or a slow shutter in bright light. [b]Note:[/b] Only has an effect when [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units] is enabled.

Time for shutter to open and close, evaluated as [code]1 / shutter_speed[/code] seconds. A higher value will allow less light (leading to a darker image), while a lower value will allow more light (leading to a brighter image). Only available when [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units] is enabled. It also sets the length of [member CameraAttributes.motion_blur_enabled] (see [member motion_blur_use_shutter_speed]), with or without physical light units, and is shown in the inspector whenever it does.

Override value for [member Camera3D.far]. Used internally when calculating depth of field. When attached to a [Camera3D] as its [member Camera3D.attributes], it will override the [member Camera3D.far] property.

Distance between camera lens and camera aperture, measured in millimeters. Controls field of view and depth of field. A larger focal length will result in a smaller field of view and a narrower depth of field meaning fewer objects will be in focus. A smaller focal length will result in a wider field of view and a larger depth of field meaning more objects will be in focus. When attached to a [Camera3D] as its [member Camera3D.attributes], it will override the [member Camera3D.fov] property and the [member Camera3D.keep_aspect] property.
Distance from camera of object that will be in focus, measured in meters. Internally this will be clamped to be at least 1 millimeter larger than [member frustum_focal_length].

Override value for [member Camera3D.near]. Used internally when calculating depth of field. When attached to a [Camera3D] as its [member Camera3D.attributes], it will override the [member Camera3D.near] property.

The horizontal squeeze of an anamorphic lens (1.33, 1.5, 1.8 and 2.0 are common; 1.0 is a spherical lens). The lens fits a field of view this many times wider onto the sensor, so the horizontal field of view widens by the squeeze and [Camera3D] keeps it, instead of the vertical one, when the squeeze is above 1.0 (see [method is_fov_horizontal]). Automatic distortion and diffraction take the squeeze into account.

How much the field of view changes with [member frustum_focus_distance]. [code]1.0[/code] is a lens that focuses by moving as a whole (most stills primes): it frames like a longer lens up close, by [code]f² / (u - f)[/code] at focus distance [code]u[/code]. [code]0.0[/code] is a cinema lens built not to breathe, and negative values a lens whose field of view widens at close focus, as many internally focusing zooms do.
The lens's largest aperture (smallest f-number). Optical vignetting ([member CameraAttributes.vignetting_enabled]) is strongest at this aperture and gone two stops smaller.

The light the lens's glass loses, in stops: the difference between its T-stop and its f-stop ([code]T = N * 2^(loss / 2)[/code]). Darkens the exposure only; depth of field and diffraction keep the f-number. Cinema lenses are marked in T-stops; a typical lens loses 0.1-0.3 stops. [b]Note:[/b] Only has an effect when [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units] is enabled.

If [code]true[/code], [member CameraAttributes.motion_blur_enabled] uses the exposure time of [member exposure_shutter_speed] as a real camera does: a [code]1/50[/code] s shutter blurs 1.2 frames' worth of motion at 60 FPS and 0.6 at 120 FPS, and [code]1/2000[/code] s almost none. This works whether or not [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units] is enabled; without it, the shutter speed only sets the blur. If [code]false[/code], [member CameraAttributes.motion_blur_shutter_angle] sets the exposure time as a fraction of each frame instead.

The size of the sensor or film frame, which sets the field of view of [member frustum_focal_length], the circle of confusion of depth of field, the size of film grain ([member CameraAttributes.grain_enabled]) and the lens effects that depend on the frame. Picking a format sets [member sensor_size].
The width and height of the sensor in millimeters. Editable when [member sensor_format] is [constant SENSOR_FORMAT_CUSTOM]; setting another size makes the format custom.
The direction of the tilt's axis in the frame, in degrees counterclockwise: [code]0.0[/code] tilts about a horizontal axis (a horizontal band of focus), [code]90.0[/code] about a vertical one.

If [code]true[/code], the lens is tilted against the sensor ([member tilt_shift_tilt]), so the plane of sharp focus tilts with it (the Scheimpflug principle). Depth of field then measures every pixel's defocus from that plane: a forward tilt brings a whole receding ground plane into focus, a reverse tilt ([member tilt_shift_tilt] negative) leaves a thin band sharp and makes a real scene look like a miniature. The plane's angle follows from the tilt, the focal length and [member frustum_focus_distance] (the hinge rule), as on a tilt-shift lens. Depth of field runs even where the untilted lens would be sharp everywhere. [b]Note:[/b] Only supported in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods. Compatibility has no depth of field. An orthogonal [Camera3D] ignores it.

The lens's tilt in degrees. Positive tilts the plane of focus so that the bottom of the frame is focused nearer than the top (along a ground plane); negative does the opposite. Tilt-shift lenses tilt up to about 8 to 15 degrees; small tilts already tilt the plane of focus steeply, more so with longer focus distances.

constants.constant: A custom size, set with [member sensor_size].
Represents the size of the [enum SensorFormat] enum.
